summary: The claim and proof are correct. Singleton rows, empty families of nontrivial rows, unequal positive endpoint weights, centers that are endpoints of other rows, and lower-dimensional supports introduce no exception. The elementary cosh estimate proves the row bound (15), and endpoint disjointness gives the uniform q-weighted variance bound 9 even when a point also serves as a center. Reflection pairing applies to every original ambient closed halfspace, and the exact likelihood and normalization identities retain the original product law throughout. The two Jensen and Cauchy-Schwarz steps give the stated constants, and the cubic bound follows under that same law. The predecessor definitions and product identity match exactly. For the chain supports, the supplied exact block completion, parity recovery of spike sources, and injectivity of the successor map establish precisely the required triple rows and disjoint endpoint sets for every permitted partition.
